title: 2 Samuel 17: The Counsel of the Lord Shall Stand
body:
Read the chapter → [2 Samuel 17](/bible/2-samuel/17)

## Introduction

This session covers [2 Samuel 17](/bible/2-samuel/17) through 20: Ahithophel's counsel against David and Hushai's counter counsel, the great battle in the wood of Ephraim and the death of Absalom, David's mourning and his return to Jerusalem, and the revolt of Sheba the son of Bichri. The thread running through all four chapters is that the devices in a man's heart are many, but the counsel of the Lord, that shall stand. Absalom moved in the spirit of deceit and betrayal against his own father, and the enemies a man of Israel must forgive are the enemies of his own people, even those risen up out of his own house.

**[2 Samuel 17:1-3](/bible/2-samuel/17#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/2-samuel/17#v1)</sup> Moreover Ahithophel said unto Absalom, Let me now choose out twelve thousand men, and I will arise and pursue after David this night:
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/2-samuel/17#v2)</sup> And I will come upon him while he is weary and weak handed, and will make him afraid: and all the people that are with him shall flee; and I will smite the king only:
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/2-samuel/17#v3)</sup> And I will bring back all the people unto thee: the man whom thou seekest is as if all returned: so all the people shall be in peace.

- Ahithophel had already given Absalom wicked counsel in the previous chapter, telling him to go in unto his father's concubines in the sight of all Israel so that the hands of all that were with him would be made strong. Ahithophel was David's own counselor turned traitor, being the devil the Bible speaks of, working deceit and betrayal from inside the gates of Israel.
- His counsel in those days was regarded as if a man had inquired at the oracle of God. That tells you Ahithophel was very influential and had the gift of gab, so persuasive that his advice sounded almost biblical.
- Now he asks Absalom to let him choose out twelve thousand men to pursue David that same night while David was weary and weak handed, to smite the king only and bring back all the people. He wanted the victory and the bragging rights of being the one who killed King David.

  Precepts:
  - **[2 Samuel 16:20-23](/bible/2-samuel/16#v20)**
    > <sup>[20](/bible/2-samuel/16#v20)</sup> Then said Absalom to Ahithophel, Give counsel among you what we shall do.
    >
    > <sup>[21](/bible/2-samuel/16#v21)</sup> And Ahithophel said unto Absalom, Go in unto thy father’s concubines, which he hath left to keep the house; and all Israel shall hear that thou art abhorred of thy father: then shall the hands of all that are with thee be strong.
    >
    > <sup>[22](/bible/2-samuel/16#v22)</sup> So they spread Absalom a tent upon the top of the house; and Absalom went in unto his father’s concubines in the sight of all Israel.
    >
    > <sup>[23](/bible/2-samuel/16#v23)</sup> And the counsel of Ahithophel, which he counselled in those days, was as if a man had enquired at the oracle of God: so was all the counsel of Ahithophel both with David and with Absalom.

    Ahithophel's counsel to defile David's concubines, and how his counsel was esteemed as the oracle of God with both David and Absalom.
  - **[Micah 2:8](/bible/micah/2#v8)**
    > <sup>[8](/bible/micah/2#v8)</sup> Even of late my people is risen up as an enemy: ye pull off the robe with the garment from them that pass by securely as men averse from war.

    The Most High's own people rise up as an enemy; the enemies Christ said to forgive are the enemies of our people.

**[2 Samuel 17:5-14](/bible/2-samuel/17#v5)**

> <sup>[5](/bible/2-samuel/17#v5)</sup> Then said Absalom, Call now Hushai the Archite also, and let us hear likewise what he saith.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/2-samuel/17#v6)</sup> And when Hushai was come to Absalom, Absalom spake unto him, saying, Ahithophel hath spoken after this manner: shall we do after his saying? if not; speak thou.
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/2-samuel/17#v7)</sup> And Hushai said unto Absalom, The counsel that Ahithophel hath given is not good at this time.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/2-samuel/17#v8)</sup> For, said Hushai, thou knowest thy father and his men, that they be mighty men, and they be chafed in their minds, as a bear robbed of her whelps in the field: and thy father is a man of war, and will not lodge with the people.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/2-samuel/17#v9)</sup> Behold, he is hid now in some pit, or in some other place: and it will come to pass, when some of them be overthrown at the first, that whosoever heareth it will say, There is a slaughter among the people that follow Absalom.
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/2-samuel/17#v10)</sup> And he also that is valiant, whose heart is as the heart of a lion, shall utterly melt: for all Israel knoweth that thy father is a mighty man, and they which be with him are valiant men.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/2-samuel/17#v11)</sup> Therefore I counsel that all Israel be generally gathered unto thee, from Dan even to Beer–sheba, as the sand that is by the sea for multitude; and that thou go to battle in thine own person.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/2-samuel/17#v12)</sup> So shall we come upon him in some place where he shall be found, and we will light upon him as the dew falleth on the ground: and of him and of all the men that are with him there shall not be left so much as one.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/2-samuel/17#v13)</sup> Moreover, if he be gotten into a city, then shall all Israel bring ropes to that city, and we will draw it into the river, until there be not one small stone found there.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/2-samuel/17#v14)</sup> And Absalom and all the men of Israel said, The counsel of Hushai the Archite is better than the counsel of Ahithophel. For the Lord had appointed to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel, to the intent that the Lord might bring evil upon Absalom.

- Absalom wanted a second opinion, so he called Hushai the Archite to hear likewise what he would say. There is safety in a multitude of counselors, but only where the counsel is according to thus saith the Lord; a counselor who does not go to the scriptures is not one you should want.
- Hushai told Absalom that Ahithophel's counsel was not good at this time. He reminded him that his father and his mighty men were mighty and chafed in their minds as a bear robbed of her whelps, war ready and strategic, and that David would not lodge with the people but move by night.
- Hushai warned that if Absalom's men were overthrown at the first, even the most valiant warrior whose heart is as the heart of a lion would utterly melt, for all Israel knew David was a mighty man. This shows David and his mighty men were on another level; none of Absalom's thousands could compare to them.
- Instead Hushai counseled that all Israel be gathered from Dan to Beersheba as the sand by the sea, with Absalom going to battle in his own person. This deliberately inaccurate counsel would waste time gathering troops and give David room to escape; Hushai was a counterintelligence agent, a spy planted in righteousness, always siding with King David.
- Absalom and all the men of Israel said Hushai's counsel was better than Ahithophel's. The Lord had appointed to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel, to the intent that He might bring evil upon Absalom. The Lord was working with Hushai and David, while Satan was in the spirit of Absalom and Ahithophel.

  Precepts:
  - **[2 Samuel 15:32-37](/bible/2-samuel/15#v32)**
    > <sup>[32](/bible/2-samuel/15#v32)</sup> And it came to pass, that when David was come to the top of the mount, where he worshipped God, behold, Hushai the Archite came to meet him with his coat rent, and earth upon his head:
    >
    > <sup>[33](/bible/2-samuel/15#v33)</sup> Unto whom David said, If thou passest on with me, then thou shalt be a burden unto me:
    >
    > <sup>[34](/bible/2-samuel/15#v34)</sup> But if thou return to the city, and say unto Absalom, I will be thy servant, O king; as I have been thy father’s servant hitherto, so will I now also be thy servant: then mayest thou for me defeat the counsel of Ahithophel.
    >
    > <sup>[35](/bible/2-samuel/15#v35)</sup> And hast thou not there with thee Zadok and Abiathar the priests? therefore it shall be, that what thing soever thou shalt hear out of the king’s house, thou shalt tell it to Zadok and Abiathar the priests.
    >
    > <sup>[36](/bible/2-samuel/15#v36)</sup> Behold, they have there with them their two sons, Ahimaaz Zadok’s son, and Jonathan Abiathar’s son; and by them ye shall send unto me every thing that ye can hear.
    >
    > <sup>[37](/bible/2-samuel/15#v37)</sup> So Hushai David’s friend came into the city, and Absalom came into Jerusalem.

    David sends Hushai back to Absalom to defeat Ahithophel's counsel and to report through Zadok and Abiathar; the name Hushai means loyal to the king.
  - **[2 Samuel 15:1-4](/bible/2-samuel/15#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/2-samuel/15#v1)</sup> And it came to pass after this, that Absalom prepared him chariots and horses, and fifty men to run before him.
    >
    > <sup>[2](/bible/2-samuel/15#v2)</sup> And Absalom rose up early, and stood beside the way of the gate: and it was so, that when any man that had a controversy came to the king for judgment, then Absalom called unto him, and said, Of what city art thou? And he said, Thy servant is of one of the tribes of Israel.
    >
    > <sup>[3](/bible/2-samuel/15#v3)</sup> And Absalom said unto him, See, thy matters are good and right; but there is no man deputed of the king to hear thee.
    >
    > <sup>[4](/bible/2-samuel/15#v4)</sup> Absalom said moreover, Oh that I were made judge in the land, that every man which hath any suit or cause might come unto me, and I would do him justice!

    Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel at the gate, promising he would do them justice if he were made judge.
  - **[1 Corinthians 12:18](/bible/1-corinthians/12#v18)**
    > <sup>[18](/bible/1-corinthians/12#v18)</sup> But now hath God set the members every one of them in the body, as it hath pleased him.

    God set the members every one in the body as it pleased Him; promotion comes from the Most High, not from a man taking the seat himself.
  - **[Proverbs 19:21](/bible/proverbs/19#v21)**
    > <sup>[21](/bible/proverbs/19#v21)</sup> There are many devices in a man’s heart; nevertheless the counsel of the Lord, that shall stand.

    There are many devices in a man's heart, but the counsel of the Lord, that shall stand.

**[2 Samuel 17:15-22](/bible/2-samuel/17#v15)**

> <sup>[15](/bible/2-samuel/17#v15)</sup> Then said Hushai unto Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, Thus and thus did Ahithophel counsel Absalom and the elders of Israel; and thus and thus have I counselled.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/2-samuel/17#v16)</sup> Now therefore send quickly, and tell David, saying, Lodge not this night in the plains of the wilderness, but speedily pass over; lest the king be swallowed up, and all the people that are with him.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/2-samuel/17#v17)</sup> Now Jonathan and Ahimaaz stayed by En–rogel; for they might not be seen to come into the city: and a wench went and told them; and they went and told king David.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/2-samuel/17#v18)</sup> Nevertheless a lad saw them, and told Absalom: but they went both of them away quickly, and came to a man’s house in Bahurim, which had a well in his court; whither they went down.
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/2-samuel/17#v19)</sup> And the woman took and spread a covering over the well’s mouth, and spread ground corn thereon; and the thing was not known.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/2-samuel/17#v20)</sup> And when Absalom’s servants came to the woman to the house, they said, Where is Ahimaaz and Jonathan? And the woman said unto them, They be gone over the brook of water. And when they had sought and could not find them, they returned to Jerusalem.
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/2-samuel/17#v21)</sup> And it came to pass, after they were departed, that they came up out of the well, and went and told king David, and said unto David, Arise, and pass quickly over the water: for thus hath Ahithophel counselled against you.
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/2-samuel/17#v22)</sup> Then David arose, and all the people that were with him, and they passed over Jordan: by the morning light there lacked not one of them that was not gone over Jordan.

- Hushai reported both Ahithophel's counsel and his own to Zadok and Abiathar the priests, telling them to send quickly and warn David not to lodge in the plains of the wilderness that night but to pass over speedily, lest he be swallowed up.
- The messengers Jonathan and Ahimaaz waited by En-rogel; a maidservant carried the word to them, but a lad saw them and told Absalom. The Most High put His spirit on certain people to orchestrate His plan; often when a man tries to do evil to another, it falls back on him, for he that diggeth a pit shall fall therein.
- They fled to a man's house in Bahurim that had a well, and a woman spread a covering over the well's mouth and ground corn upon it to camouflage it. When Absalom's servants came asking, she told them the men had gone over the brook of water, and the pursuers returned to Jerusalem.
- The two came up out of the well and told David to arise and pass quickly over the water. David and all the people passed over Jordan by the morning light, and there lacked not one of them that was not gone over.

  Precepts:
  - **[Psalms 3:1-8](/bible/psalms/3#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/psalms/3#v1)</sup> Lord, how are they increased that trouble me! many are they that rise up against me.
    >
    > <sup>[2](/bible/psalms/3#v2)</sup> Many there be which say of my soul, There is no help for him in God. Selah.
    >
    > <sup>[3](/bible/psalms/3#v3)</sup> But thou, O Lord, art a shield for me; my glory, and the lifter up of mine head.
    >
    > <sup>[4](/bible/psalms/3#v4)</sup> I cried unto the Lord with my voice, and he heard me out of his holy hill. Selah.
    >
    > <sup>[5](/bible/psalms/3#v5)</sup> I laid me down and slept; I awaked; for the Lord sustained me.
    >
    > <sup>[6](/bible/psalms/3#v6)</sup> I will not be afraid of ten thousands of people, that have set themselves against me round about.
    >
    > <sup>[7](/bible/psalms/3#v7)</sup> Arise, O Lord; save me, O my God: for thou hast smitten all mine enemies upon the cheek bone; thou hast broken the teeth of the ungodly.
    >
    > <sup>[8](/bible/psalms/3#v8)</sup> Salvation belongeth unto the Lord: thy blessing is upon thy people. Selah.

    A Psalm of David when he fled from Absalom his son; the Lord is a shield for him, sustaining him in sleep though ten thousands set themselves against him.

**[2 Samuel 17:23](/bible/2-samuel/17#v23)**

> <sup>[23](/bible/2-samuel/17#v23)</sup> And when Ahithophel saw that his counsel was not followed, he saddled his ass, and arose, and gat him home to his house, to his city, and put his household in order, and hanged himself, and died, and was buried in the sepulchre of his father.

- When Ahithophel saw that his counsel was not followed, he set his house in order and hanged himself. The evil counsel he devised reared its head around and bit its author; evil pursueth sinners, but to the righteous good shall be repaid.
- To be righteous is to observe to do all the commandments of the Lord; all unrighteousness is sin, and sin is the transgression of the law. David was righteous and did not want to war against his own son, yet good was repaid to him, while the sinner was pursued by his own evil.

  Precepts:
  - **[Proverbs 13:21](/bible/proverbs/13#v21)**
    > <sup>[21](/bible/proverbs/13#v21)</sup> Evil pursueth sinners: but to the righteous good shall be repayed.

    Evil pursueth sinners, but to the righteous good shall be repaid.
  - **[Deuteronomy 6:25](/bible/deuteronomy/6#v25)**
    > <sup>[25](/bible/deuteronomy/6#v25)</sup> And it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments before the Lord our God, as he hath commanded us.

    It shall be our righteousness if we observe to do all these commandments before the Lord.
  - **[1 John 5:17](/bible/1-john/5#v17)**
    > <sup>[17](/bible/1-john/5#v17)</sup> All unrighteousness is sin: and there is a sin not unto death.

    All unrighteousness is sin; to be unrighteous is to not keep the commandments.
